Hi all —

Quick note ahead of Monday's alignment call on evaluation methodology. Wanted to surface our recommended approach so you have context:

1) Offline evaluation (recommended first step)
- Purpose: fast signal on quality before touching production.
- Plan: human grading of ~200 holdout samples from the anonymized set. Graders: 3 internal graders + 1 Acme SME where available.
- Rubric (example):
  - Usefulness (0-2): 0=no useful info, 1=partial, 2=fully actionable
  - Faithfulness (0-2): 0=incorrect/hallucinated facts, 1=minor inaccuracy, 2=accurate
  - Conciseness (0-1): 0=too verbose, 1=concise
  - Overall pass = (Usefulness + Faithfulness + Conciseness) >= 4 (out of 5)
- Target: >= 80% pass rate on holdout to proceed to shadowing.

2) Online shadow / live evaluation
- Purpose: measure real-world acceptability and operational characteristics.
- Plan: run 3 business days of shadow for one agent queue (no customer-visible changes). Collect: agent acceptance edits, latency P95, failure/error rates, rate of rerank/corrections.

- Success thresholds: agent acceptance >= 80%, latency P95 < 500ms, hallucination incidents < 2% over shadow period.

3) Grading logistics and ownership
- Marissa: lead rubric onboarding & grader training, coordinate with Acme SME for tie-breaks.
- Rachel: implement metrics instrumentation (agent edit tracking, latency histograms) and deliver dashboard link.
- Timeline: offline grading complete by 2027-03-19; shadow run 2027-03-22 to 2027-03-24 (contingent on sample vetting).

Open questions for Acme (to discuss Mon):
- Are Acme SMEs available to join a 1-hour grader calibration session (we recommend 3/16 or 3/17)?
- Any internal constraints around running a shadow on the selected queue (business hours, agents to include)?

I attached a short grading template (tab in the attached XLSX) and a sample rubric PDF. Please review and we'll finalize on Monday.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Eval & Applied ML | Redwood Inference
